display.purpose: The cafe name in the hero. Appears exactly once per page.

headline.purpose: Section titles. Centred on full-width sections, left-aligned beside a photo column.

title.purpose: Standalone short statements: the address block, the form's sent confirmation.

subtitle.purpose: Menu item names — a product name as a heading in miniature.

body-lead.purpose: The hero's single supporting line, capped at ~24rem measure.

body.purpose: Section prose, capped at ~28rem measure or by half-column width.

label.purpose: Form labels, list terms, prices, descriptions, buttons, nav links. The workhorse size.

micro.purpose: Variant lists, caffeine reading, decorative footer badges.

toneSystem.purpose: Sections alternate light paper and dark walnut grounds; components read --tone-* variables so one component renders on either field.

shadows.name: framed-media
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. Sits under photo and map frames so they read as objects on the table. On dark grounds the same geometry is tinted near-black: 0 18px 40px -24px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.8).

motion.name: state-color
motion.purpose: Every interactive state change. Colour only — no lift, scale, or shadow.

motion.name: photo-settle
motion.purpose: Menu card photography on hover, clipped by its frame. The single non-instant motion in the system.

motion.name: anchor-scroll
motion.purpose: Nav links and the hero CTA. No entrance animations exist anywhere.

texture.name: grain-light
texture.value: SVG fractalNoise baseFrequency 0.85, 3 octaves, 140x140 tile; opacity 0.055; mix-blend-mode: multiply
texture.purpose: Overlay on every light ground so paper reads as material, not flat fill. Non-interactive.

texture.name: grain-dark
texture.value: SVG fractalNoise baseFrequency 0.85, 3 octaves, 140x140 tile; opacity 0.07; mix-blend-mode: overlay
texture.purpose: Overlay on every dark ground so walnut reads as worn wood.

browserSurfaces.name: selection
browserSurfaces.purpose: Text selection is themed brass on deep walnut.

browserSurfaces.name: scrollbar
browserSurfaces.purpose: Walnut thumb on a paper track.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The only button style in the system: an outlined pill that fully inverts on hover. Used for the hero CTA, Get Directions, and Send Message.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: #7a5219; background: transparent; border: 1px solid rgb(59 42 30 / 0.3); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 12px 28px; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms, background-color 150ms, border-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #3b2a1e; color: #e4d9c0; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b8863b; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; background: transparent; color: #7a5219; }

components.name: Primary Button (dark ground)
components.description: The same button rendered on a walnut section — proof that one component works on either field via the tone variables.

components.name: Menu Category Tab
components.description: Square catalog-divider tabs. The selected tab fully inverts to the heading colour; inactive tabs are hairline outlines. Deliberately not brass.

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Library-slip form field: square, hairline stroke over a lighter paper fill, label above. Focus shifts the border to the tone accent.

components.name: Sticky Navigation
components.description: Fixed page chrome, permanently on the paper ground: a centred row of five text links with a scroll-derived brass active state. No hamburger at any width.

components.css: .ds-card { width: 260px; background: #3b2a1e; padding: 20px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-card-frame { border: 4px solid #2a1d13; overflow: hidden; } .ds-card-photo { aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #5c4430, #2a1d13); transition: transform 700ms cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-card:hover .ds-card-photo { transform: scale(1.05); } .ds-card-text { margin-top: 16px; } .ds-card-row { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; } .ds-card-name { font-family: Vollkorn, Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: 1.125rem; color: #e4d9c0; margin: 0; } .ds-card-price { font-size: 0.875rem; color: #c4b192; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-card-desc { font-size: 0.875rem; color: #c4b192; margin: 6px 0 0; } .ds-card-meta { margin-top: 10px; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 4px 16px; } .ds-card-variants { font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.025em; color: #c4b192; } .ds-meter { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; } .ds-meter-label { font-size: 0.75rem; color: #c4b192; } .ds-meter-dots { display: flex; gap: 2px; } .ds-meter-dots i { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgb(228 217 192 / 0.2); } .ds-meter-dots i.on { background: #d9a752; }

components.name: Framed Media
components.description: The signature mount: a solid 8px walnut frame with 4px interior padding, a fixed 4:5 ratio, and the system's single soft shadow. No image in the build is full-bleed or text-overlaid.

narrative.overview:
The world is an old university library's reading room after the afternoon has gone quiet: worn walnut tables, aged paper, a single brass banker's lamp, and no urgency anywhere. The page is built to feel like a room you sit down in rather than a storefront that sells at you. Density is generous and unhurried — sections breathe at 96–128px of vertical air, copy stays in short measured columns, and nothing blinks, badges, or shouts.

The most load-bearing decision in the built system is that the page has two grounds, not one. Sections alternate a light paper field and a dark walnut field, and every component inside main reads --tone-* variables instead of naming a colour. One card, one button, one rule line renders correctly on either field. This exists because the first build put everything on a single cream ground and read as flat and empty across every viewport — the alternation is structure, not decoration, and it is what makes the "dim room" actually dim.

The aesthetic is fixed. It does not respond to prefers-color-scheme; a reading room is the temperature it is. Two clusters are explicitly rejected: the generic AI-landing-page look (cream ground, italic display serif, terracotta accent) and the bright, high-saturation, aggressively-zoomed product-photo style of commercial chain cafés. Green and any high-saturation hue are out of the palette entirely.
keyCharacteristics: Two alternating grounds — paper light, walnut dark — driven by a tone-variable layer
One accent (brass), reserved for active and focused states only
Serif display (Vollkorn, regular weight, tight tracking) over sans body (Inter)
Square corners everywhere except pill buttons and status dots
A visible grain overlay on every ground, so colour fields read as material
Flat by default; the only shadow in the system sits under framed photography

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Sections alternate tone-light and tone-dark down the page — never two of the same tone in sequence. Components inside main read --tone-bg, --tone-heading, --tone-body, --tone-accent, --tone-rule, --tone-frame, --tone-field-bg, --tone-field-border, --tone-hover-bg, --tone-hover-fg. A hardcoded colour inside a section component is a bug.

rules.name: The Contrast-Bound Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent is tone-dependent for legibility, not for effect. Plain brass on the paper ground measures 2.3:1 and fails AA; light sections therefore use brass-deep and dark sections brass-glow. Do not collapse these back into one brass value. Plain brass is permitted only on the browser surfaces where it sits against walnut-deep (selection) or acts as a ring rather than text (focus outline).

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Brass marks state — active, selected, focused, filled — and nothing else. If an element is neither active nor focused, it is wood, paper, or ink. No green; no high-saturation hue of any kind enters the palette.

rules.name: The Fixed Room Rule
rules.body: The aesthetic does not adapt to system light/dark preference. There is no prefers-color-scheme branch and none should be added; the tone system already carries both temperatures deliberately.

rules.name: The Serif-For-Nouns Rule
rules.body: Vollkorn is for names of things — the café, the sections, the drinks, the address. Everything a reader scans or acts on (labels, prices, descriptions, buttons, nav) is Inter. Never set body prose in the display face.

rules.name: The Regular-Weight Rule
rules.body: Display type earns emphasis from size and tracking, never from weight. Vollkorn is used at 400 throughout; bold and italic display settings are loaded by the font link but unused, and should stay that way.

rules.name: The No Shouting Rule
rules.body: There is no uppercase type anywhere in the system, and no tracked-out eyebrow or kicker above any heading. Sections open directly on their headline. Letter-spacing above zero appears only at 0.025em on labels and micro text, to keep small sans readable — never as a decorative device.

rules.name: The Flat-Except-Frames Rule
rules.body: Nothing is elevated except framed media. Interactive elements respond by changing colour, never by lifting, glowing, or gaining a shadow. There are no hard offset shadows anywhere in this world and none should be introduced.

rules.name: The Grain Rule
rules.body: Every ground carries the grain overlay via tone-light / tone-dark. A new full-bleed surface joins the tone system rather than setting its own background colour, or it will read as a flat patch against a textured page.

dos: Do wrap any new full-width section in tone-light or tone-dark and alternate it against its neighbour, so the page keeps its light/dark rhythm and inherits the grain overlay.
Do read colours from the --tone-* variables inside section components; a new component should render correctly on either ground without a conditional.
Do keep the accent tone-dependent — brass-deep (4.9:1) on paper, brass-glow (6.3:1) on walnut.
Do reserve brass for active, selected, focused, and filled states only.
Do set names of things in Vollkorn at weight 400 with -0.02em tracking, and everything scannable or clickable in Inter.
Do pad new sections 96px vertically, 128px at md, inside the 64rem container with 24px gutters.
Do mount imagery in the solid --tone-frame border with its fixed aspect ratio and the single Framed Media shadow.
Do design the empty, sending, error, and success states of any new interaction in the existing palette — no new colour is needed for failure.
Do keep corners square, reserving pills for buttons and circles for status dots.
donts: Don't hardcode a hex or Tailwind colour class inside a section component; that breaks tone portability. (Nav and footer are the deliberate, already-recorded exception.)
Don't collapse brass-deep and brass-glow into a single brass, and don't put plain brass (#b8863b) on the paper ground as text — it measures 2.3:1 and fails AA.
Don't add a prefers-color-scheme branch; the aesthetic is fixed by design.
Don't introduce green or any high-saturation hue, including a red error colour.
Don't add shadows to buttons, cards, tabs, or fields, and don't add hard offset shadows anywhere — the Framed Media shadow is the entire vocabulary.
Don't add an uppercase tracked kicker, eyebrow, or category label above a heading; sections open on their headline.
Don't use italic or bold Vollkorn for display type, and don't reach for a second accent when a hierarchy feels weak — increase size or space instead.
Don't hide menu item details (price, description, variants, caffeine) behind hover; the primary audience is on touchscreens where hover does not exist.
Don't use entrance animations or motion that delays reading. Transitions are colour-only at ~150ms; the 700ms photo scale on hover is the single deliberate exception and it is not a load effect.
Don't add a second button variant. If a second action is needed on a screen, demote it to a text link — the UX floor allows one obvious primary action per screen.
